newsitem.title: USA: McNeil Real Estate Fund XXVII rejects buyout offer.
newsitem.headline: McNeil Real Estate Fund XXVII rejects buyout offer.

text.p: McNeil Real Estate Fund XXVII, LP said on Thursday that it received and rejected an unsolicited offer to acquire all outstanding units of the partnership at $6.50 per unit from an unaffiliated third party.
The offer, which is not conditioned on receipt of financing or due diligence, was made by a privately held real estate company, said a statement from McNeil that did not name the party.
After meeting with the offerer in Dallas and considering the $6.50 offer, the partnership said it had rejected it as being inadequate.

The partnership said that this offer closely follows one by Carl Icahn to buy all units of the Partnership for $5.62 per unit. On Oct. 4, 1996, the partnership said it determined that Icahn's offer was inadequate.
The partnership said its financial advisor, Crosson Dannis Inc estimated that the present liquidation value of the partnership's units was between $8.37 and $8.64 per unit.
